## Session log — 2026-09-03/05 (bug-hunt wave 9: 8 findings, all 8 FIXED and post-merge verified; plus one test-infra gap, W9-9)

**Shape of the pass.** Six agents over disjoint domains (airlock/capture, cancel/defer/recover/generators,
channel/nursery/Shared/Executor, checker⊋compiler, core language, stdlib+CLI), ~450 probe programs, each
finding re-verified by the main loop on the release binary before filing. Every ticket was then judged at
its plan gate and every merged fix re-run on the merged binary rather than trusted from the gate — which
`docs/gaps.md`'s own history says is required (`auto-task review unreliable`).

**The mechanical oracles found nothing, and that is the headline.** Run beyond their CI ranges:
panic-fuzz seeds `2000..25000` → 0 findings in 23 000; the CPython differential seeds `5000..12000` →
0 in 7 000; `--floats` seeds `20000..26000` → 0 in 6 000; the 7 FFI goldens → 0. Large curated
surfaces were byte-identical to CPython: 1160 format specs (Chezzi statically rejects 325 and CPython
raises on exactly those 325), 400 unicode string-method cases, 400 base64/hex/url, 400 CSV, 510
datetime, 432 regex, 300 JSON round-trips. **All eight findings came from hand-built adversarial
programs judged against a RUN reference program**, not from generators — the same lesson W8 recorded:
a green suite measures the assertions you thought to write.

**What the eight were.** Three silent wrong answers (W9-1 airlock third copy, W9-3 `eq` bound
laundered through a protocol slot, W9-5 the newtype/DEC-029 inconsistency), one silent hang at the
default worker count (W9-2 Executor), three false rejections of programs the ancestors accept (W9-4
expected-type sinks, W9-6 turbofish forwarding, W9-8 BOM), and one wrong-position family (W9-7 JSON).
**None was reachable by the standing gates**: a silent wrong answer has no assertion to fail, a hang
has no exit code to check, and a message position no test reads.

**One filed ticket was WRONG, and the pipeline caught it, not the hunt.** W9-5 as filed claimed the
duplicate-declaration guard missed `struct S` + `fn S`. That pair is DEC-029, active and shipped in
`std/path.chz`; the filed fix would have deleted a working feature. The planning stage refused the
premise and asked. **The lesson is the one already in this file for closed rows: read the decision
records before filing, and read a closed row's PRESCRIPTION before implementing it.** What survived
was narrower and real — `newtype` was the lone host disagreeing with DEC-029.

**A subagent's measurement was also wrong, in the direction that would have blocked a good fix.** The
implementing stage for W9-2 reported a race its own change had introduced, with `0/30` on base against
`3/30` on branch. Re-measured by the main loop at 40 repeats each: **branch 3/40, main 2/40** — no
delta, and the test (`try_recv_drains_residue_after_blocking_recv_resumes`) was already the twelfth
name on TICKET-050's deferred list. A 30-sample run that misses a ~5% flake reads as proof of zero.
**Corollary for any future flake comparison: size the sample so a 5% rate cannot read as 0, and check
the failing test's NAME against the known-flaky list before reasoning about its shape.**

**The pass's largest cost was environmental, not technical.** Four tickets escalated on a RED suite
that had nothing to do with them, because the dispatcher had been started under a supervisor missing
`pipeline run -j 1`, so stages ran cargo concurrently on 12 cores. `.project/run-supervised.sh` is the
supervisor of record and already handles this (it also distinguishes the deliberate
"dispatcher source changed" exit from a human stop). Once stages were serialised, `bash
.project/run-test.sh` on the same base the gate had called RED exited **0**, every target green. The
three tests that reddened under load are W9-9.

**Doc drift fixed in place rather than ticketed** (commit `b0c76e52`): the retired generator
reach-gate claim in `docs/syntax.md:1438` and `docs/future.md:793` (the reach-gate + poison-snapshot
model was retired 2026-07-21; a module-global generator crosses BY VALUE); the `RwShared` example at
`docs/concurrency.md:603` that did not compile (`insert` is a List method, `sum_values` never
existed); and the `cancelled()` complexity claim in `std/cancel.chz:34`, `docs/stdlib.md` and
`docs/concurrency.md`, which said **O(depth), ~0.29 µs per ancestor** while the measured cost is
QUADRATIC — 0.53 µs at depth 0, 178 µs at 100, **2360 µs at 400** — against Go's flat O(1) `ctx.Err()`.
`docs/benchmarks.md:1859` had recorded the superlinearity and its cause all along; only the
user-facing claims were stale. That is the standing pattern: **a constant measured at depth ≤ 5 does
not describe the curve.**


## Session log — 2026-08-18 (`W8-43` — the structural-depth budget is now SHARED across nested protocol-hook re-entries)

**One row, filed already-CLOSED.** Found while working the wave-9 backlog, not by a gate. A user
`eq`/`str` hook dispatched from inside a native structural walk re-entered the VM and started a FRESH
depth-0 walk, so neither guard could fire — call depth stayed far below its 10 000 cap while the
*product* of hook-nesting depth × per-hook walk depth grew without bound, and the process died by
host stack overflow. Measured on `target/release/chezzi` at `c97d24ff`, `ulimit -v 12000000`:

| program | pre-fix | post-fix | CPython 3.14 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Leaf.eq` comparing two fresh 100-link chains, nested **5 000** deep | `fatal runtime error: stack overflow, aborting`, **rc=134**, core dumped, `still alive` never printed | `still alive`, **rc=0**, recoverable `maximum structural depth (10000) exceeded` | catchable `RecursionError: Stack overflow (used 8148 kB) in comparison`, rc=0 |
| the same at nesting **200** | prints `true`, **rc=0** (every level restarts at 0, so nothing faults) | recoverable `Err`, **rc=0** | `RecursionError` |

The d=200 measurement is why the regression test is scaled there rather than at 5 000: a SIGABRT
would take the whole `chz_suite_passes` gate down with it, while d=200 gives a fast, non-crashing RED
that is still ~20 000 structural levels against a 10 000 budget.

**Why nobody caught it.** The behaviour was **documented as deliberate in two source comments**
(`values_equal_guarded`'s "starts a FRESH depth-0 walk … bounded there by the call-depth guard" and
`stringify_into`'s "a `str` method re-stringifies at the *same* depth"), so every review that read
them read a design, not a defect — while `MAX_STRUCTURAL_DEPTH`'s own doc promised the opposite
("turns that into a recoverable `RuntimeError`"). Both comments are corrected in the fix commit, and
the sizing rationale at the constant now states the assumption that was false: the
`MAX_CALL_DEPTH`/`VM_STACK_BYTES` co-tuning assumes **O(1) native frames per call-depth level**,
which holds for `run_until` and for the `hash`/`compare` hooks but NOT for a structural walk nested
under a hook. **Detector coverage:** the CPython differential does classify signal-kills as findings
(since `W7-33`), but `src/difftest/generate.rs` has no user-struct-with-protocol-method feature, so a
hook-nested walk is structurally outside its corpus — this was not a tuning miss, it was out of
scope.

**The fix, and the alternative that fails.** `Vm::walk_base` carries the depth the enclosing walks
already consumed; the **5 FAULTING** `MAX_STRUCTURAL_DEPTH` comparisons test `walk_base + depth`
(including the ones that cannot themselves re-enter — each can still run *inside* a hook), and the 4
`run_proto` dispatches with a live structural
`depth` in scope go through a panic-safe `Vm::guarded_walk`. The cheaper-looking alternative —
charge `depth` to `call_depth` around each hook — **fails**, because `GenCtx` carries its own
`call_depth` and the generator resume swaps it, so a generator driven from inside a hook would swap
the charge away. A plain `Vm` field is not swapped there, which is exactly right: the generator's
frames are on the same host stack.

**The correction the first cut needed: a DEGRADING guard must not share the budget.** All seven
guards were charged initially, and two of them do not fault — `cyclic_walk` stores the map/set key by
reference, `snapshot_value` aliases the tail. Charging those two silently pushed an ORDINARY shallow
acyclic key into the degrade branch whenever it was inserted from inside a hook running at depth, so
a later mutation of the caller's value reached the stored key: `4998 -> true`, `4999 -> false` on one
and the same program, `true` at every depth pre-branch. **The general rule, worth more than the two
lines it cost: charging a stack-safety guard is only sound when its over-budget branch FAULTS.** A
faulting guard that fires early is a conservative, visible refusal; a degrading one that fires early
is a wrong answer with nothing to observe it. Both are back on the bare `depth` and pinned by
`tests/chz/spec/eq_protocol_containers_test.chz::key_inserted_from_a_deep_eq_hook_is_still_snapshotted` at both depths.

documented lints only (not re-run). Every repro is retained under the session scratchpad. Where the
report's number and this repo's number differ, **the in-repo number is the one in the row**.

### Outcome, and why the re-run mattered

| | count | rows |

**Before filing anything, all 15 open `W8-*` rows were re-run on this binary — every one still

(`p := "\\d{4}-\\d{2}"` → `\d4-\d2`), `W8-3` (all three shapes: nested `set` lost → `11`; nested `get`
reads the pre-guard `10`; nested `update` on the same box hangs, rc=124), `W8-4` (`sort_by_key`
mutations vanish → `[1, 2, 3]`), `W8-6` (`\2/\1` → `Ok('\\2/\\1')`), `W8-9` (`"100000000000h"` → `Ok`,
`"2562047788015ms"` → `Err`), `W8-10` (`chezzi run -- --dir logs` → `unknown flag '--'`), `W8-12`
(all three ISO-8601 forms still `Err`), `W8-13` (`assertion failed`, no operands), `W8-16` (the
value-slot form still withholds the missing method), `W8-17` (no suggestions anywhere), `W8-19`
(`Option[int] has no method 'unwrap_or'`), `W8-20` (`module 'json' has no member 'encode'`) — and
`W8-11`'s code facts by inspection, as before.

### The two that did NOT reproduce

Both are recorded with their measurement so the next pass does not re-chase them. Neither is filed.

- **A false `deadlock` verdict when a helper that `spawn:`s is called from a task** (the report's D3,
  measured by them at 16/25 at `threads=2`). **0 failures in 320 runs here**: the filed program *and*
  an explicit nested-nursery variant, at `--threads=1/2/3/4`, 25–30 runs each, on **both** this HEAD
  **and a purpose-built `main@088c202a` binary** — the exact commit the report names. The report's
  own framing (\"the unfixed mirror of `B5`\") is therefore unsupported on this box; if it is real it
  is machine- or load-dependent, and a repro that pins it would be worth more than the row.
- **`io.flush()` losing stdout before a crash** (their 7/100). **0/100** with an index-out-of-bounds
  fault, **0/60** with `os.exit(3)`, **0/60** with a fault inside a `spawn:` — CPython's paired
  program 0/40. Separately, the report's \"docs call it a no-op\" is not drift: `io.flush()` being an
  honest no-op on the *unbuffered* stdout sink is a deliberate documented decision
  (`docs/gaps.md:3514`, `:3728` — buffering is a value you hold).

### The dedupe that matters: wave 9's `D4`/`D5` are `W8-3`, not new rows

`W8-3` is filed as *\"`Shared.set()` inside `Shared.update()` loses the write\"* — a **same-task
reentrancy** row. Wave 9 hit the same defect from two other directions, and the three only make sense
together, so they are folded into that row rather than filed separately:

```
# (a) CROSS-TASK — the clobbering set is on ANOTHER task
s := Shared(0)
fn slow(x: int) -> int:
    time.sleep_ms(300)
    return x + 1
parallel:
    spawn: s.update(slow)              # reads 0, sleeps 300ms, writes 1
    spawn:
        time.sleep_ms(100)
        s.set(100)                     # lands mid-"RMW"
print("s = {s.get()}")                 # → s = 1        (threads 1/2/4, identical)
                                       #   Go mutex     → 100   (nothing lost)
```

```
# (b) CROSS-BOX update-in-update — hangs forever, and the docs bless this exact program
a := Shared(1); b := Shared(2)
fn bumpb(x: int) -> int: ...  b.update(...)  ...      # a's closure takes b
fn bumpa(y: int) -> int: ...  a.update(...)  ...      # b's closure takes a
parallel:
    spawn: a.update(bumpb)
    spawn: b.update(bumpa)
# → rc=124 at 1/2/4 threads, no output, no deadlock report
# docs/concurrency.md:605: "(Re-entering a *different* box, or a same-box read/get, is fine.)"
```

```
# (c) ...and --timeout cannot reach it: the same body as a `test fn`
$ chezzi test --timeout=2000 inv_test.chz     → rc=124        (the RUNNER hangs)
$ chezzi test --timeout=2000 spin_test.chz    → "1 timed out" (control: the flag works)
```

**One root cause for all of it, and it is documented as deliberate:** `docs/concurrency.md:598` says
`read`/`write` *\"copy the value out of the lock and **drop the guard before running the closure**\"* —
so `update` is not a critical section at all. Two lines above it, `:596` promises the opposite:
*\"the whole `write` is serialised so concurrent writers can't lose each other's updates.\"* The same
paragraph contradicts itself, and (a) is what that contradiction costs.

**This also re-derives `W8-3`'s filed prescription, per the CLAUDE.md convention that a closed or
open row's *Fix* column must be re-measured before it is implemented.** W8-3's fix (a) says the lost
`set` should **fault** (`set on a box already write-locked by this task`). That is right for the
same-task shape and **wrong for (a) above**, where the clobbering `set` is on a *different* task and
faulting a healthy program would be the **[[parked-is-not-stuck]]** mistake — it must **block**. And
fixing the guard makes (b) *more* reachable, not less: today the lock inversion in (b) cannot happen
through `get` precisely *because* the guard is dropped. **So the deadlock verdict in W8-3's fix (b)
has to land in the same commit as the guard**, or holding the guard converts a silent wrong answer
into a new class of hang.

### Cross-cutting themes (the reporters', re-derived here)

1. **The oracle is configured not to look.** `W8-23` sits behind a deliberate `MAX_BOUND` cap at 1e12
   in the CPython differential — the one gate that would catch it is capped just below where it
   starts. `W8-42` sits behind this file's own \"format specs: one byte differs\" line, which is true
   *of the specs the differential generates*. A differential is excellent inside its configured
   window; the window is where the bugs are not.
2. **A fix applied to some arms of an N-way set** — wave 6's meta-finding, and still the highest-yield
   lever. `W8-23` (int↔int made exact, mixed arm left behind), `W8-31` (allow-list covers
   `List`/`Map`/tuple, forgets `struct`/`enum`/`fn`), ~~`W8-37`~~ (the W8-14/W8-15 span sweep reached
   `run` and `check`, not `test` — **closed 2026-08-27**, TICKET-010). Three independent instances in
   one pass.
3. **`chezzi test` was a second-class citizen** (~~`W8-37`~~, and `W8-13` before it, both closed
   2026-08-27). `run` and `check` had coordinates, traces and JSON before the project's *own* primary
   loop did.
4. **Docs that over-claim cost more than docs that under-claim.** Every lane praised the docs, then
   was misled by one: *\"precedence follows Python\"* (`W8-28`), *\"re-entering a different box is
   fine\"* (`W8-3` (b)), *\"`Err` on an unreadable root\"* (`W8-39`), *\"`parse` → `stringify`
   round-trips\"* (`W8-35`), *\"refuses to overwrite\"* (`W8-24`). Trust earned by the good 95% is
   spent on the bad 5%.
5. **A stale binary is invisible.** The reporters' box had **no C linker**, so `cargo build` failed
   and left an eight-day-old `target/release/chezzi` in place — and the *next* `cargo` invocation
   reports `Finished` because nothing changed. This is the same family as the two traps already in
   CLAUDE.md (shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, worktree stale-binary), with a third mouth: **a build that
   FAILS also leaves a runnable binary behind**. Verify the binary contains the change, not that the
   build command exited 0.

### What came back clean (controls — the reporters', not re-run here)

Recorded because a control is evidence: slicing (567 + 400 randomized cases vs CPython, lists and
strings) 0 divergence; int arithmetic (600 randomized nested expressions, 8 operators) 0 divergence;
crypto digests + HMAC byte-identical to `hashlib` including an over-block-size key; 500-document JSON
round-trip, 1 class (`W8-35`); every 977th codepoint through base64/hex/url, 0 failures; `std.path`
vs `posixpath` over 25 adversarial paths, 1 documented diff; all 256 byte values round-trip through
`fs`; ~600 race runs (atomics, `ConcurrentMap`, fan-in, CAS retry, shared `Writer`) 0 deviation; ~40
concurrent programs at 4 worker counts, 0 schedule-dependent; ~25 deliberately-unsound programs all
rejected; 7 parser nesting shapes to n=100 000 clean; FFI (400k callback calls, null derefs, bad
signatures, GC-forcing callbacks) judged safer than `ctypes`.

## Session log — 2026-08-17 (EXTERNAL DOGFOOD PASS: 20 findings, W8-1..W8-20 — the first pass run by people who did not build this)

**What it was.** Ten independent developers, each new to Chezzi, each given one area and told to build
real programs and check every answer against the **owning ancestor** (Python / Go / Rust). Nothing was
taken on the docs' word. **343 Chezzi programs, 45 reference programs** (12 Python, 21 Go, 12 Rust) run
against `target/release/chezzi` on darwin 24.3.0 / 10 cores. Findings W8-1, W8-2, W8-4, W8-7, W8-8 were
reproduced independently by the reporters.

**PROVENANCE — read this before citing any number in this section.** The rows are a mix of three kinds
of evidence and they are not interchangeable:
- **Re-reproduced in-repo on Linux / 12 cores at `c197d128`** (a Linux number replaces the report's darwin
  number wherever the two are given): **W8-1 through W8-10 and W8-12 through W8-20** — 19 of the 20. Every
  repro in this section's code blocks and every `--threads` table below is one of these. (W8-19's
  mechanical claims were each run — the missing methods, the absent globals, `Channel[T](0)`, `wait:` on
  `accept()`, the single-expression closure; only the reporters' keyboard-cost counts inside it were not.)
- **Confirmed by the repo owner on macOS, not reproducible in-repo** (this is a Linux box): **W8-11**'s
  `dlopen` failure. The *code* facts around it — which examples name `libc.so.6`, which goldens are
  `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]` — were verified here; the runtime failure was not.
- **The reporters' measurements, taken on darwin 24.3.0 / 10 cores and NOT re-run here:** the
  strong-areas table below (except its RE2 row, marked *re-measured*), the real-app timings, the LOC
  counts, the pytest/rustc/`ctypes` comparisons, and the per-developer counts ("3 of 10 hit this").
  These are cited as the reporters' findings, not as this repo's measurements.

Three of the report's own claims **did not reproduce** and are corrected in place below rather than
carried forward: the ReDoS repro subject, `path.join`'s "double slash", and two of the diagnostics
cosmetics (see **W8-17**). **Three** of the report's line-number citations were wrong — `stdlib.md:1399`
and `gaps.md:3455` for tuple-`Hashable` (the real ones are `stdlib.md:1454` / `gaps.md:3706`), and
`src/vm/golden_tests.rs:4421` as an FFI golden (it is `read_file_caps_oversized_input`) — all replaced
with verified ones. One repro in the report **does not even compile** (W8-5's, which imports a
nonexistent `std.text`).

**Why this pass is different from waves 1–7.** Every previous wave was run by the people who wrote the
code, hunting the classes they already suspected. This one had **no model of the implementation**, so
what it found is disjoint from what the waves found: waves 1–7 are almost entirely *soundness* (a
checker accepts what the compiler can't lower, an airlock misses a guard, a scheduler verdict fires on a
healthy program). **Not one W8 row is the `checker-superset-of-compiler` class that dominates waves
1–7** — W8-2 is the nearest, and it is a missing *warning*, not an unsound accept. The rest is the layer users actually touch — silent
wrong answers, scheduler defaults, message quality, and prose that had gone stale. Neither population
of bugs is reachable from the other's method, which is the standing argument for keeping both.

### The headline, stated honestly in both directions

The semantics are in **good shape**. **The table below is the REPORTERS' evidence, darwin 10-core, not
re-run here**, except its RE2 row, marked *re-measured* — cite the rest as their finding:

| area | evidence |
|---|---|
| value semantics | 40+ CPython differentials on slicing, unicode, format specs, float repr, compound assignment — **one byte differs** (`NaN` casing, **W8-18** item 4). `{2.5:.0f}`→`2`, `{3.5:.0f}`→`4`, `0.1+0.2`→`0.30000000000000004`, `xs[4:1:-1]`, `xs[-100:]`, `"héllo wörld 😀"` char-indexed throughout |
| exhaustiveness | four deliberate sneak attempts — missing arm, hole behind `if false`, value laundered through a generic `fn pick[T](x:T)->T`, recursive enum — all caught, all naming the missing variant |
| `defer`/`panic`/`recover` | **byte-for-byte with Go** on later-panic-wins-during-unwind and panicking-cleanup-on-normal-return. Block-scoped `defer` is **better** than Go's: the loop-defer leak cannot be written. `os.exit(7)` correctly bypasses `recover:` |
| loop capture | Go-1.22 correct uniformly — `for`, `while`, `range`, nested closures, comprehensions, where Python gives `2 2 2` |
| `std.collections` | 7,000-op differential fuzz (4,000 Deque ops vs a List model, 3,000 Heap ops vs a sorted model) — **zero mismatches**. An inconsistent heap comparator neither hung nor crashed |
| `Map` / sort | insertion order CPython-exact incl. reassign-keeps-position and remove-then-readd-moves-to-end; `sort_by`/`sort_by_key` stable; `Counter.most_common` matches CPython character for character |
| `std.crypto` | every digest matches `hashlib`/`shasum` on 4 inputs incl. a 4-byte emoji string; HMAC matches on empty, normal **and 70-byte** keys — the key-hashing path where hand-rolled HMACs break |
| `std.math`/`csv`/`path` | 25/25 math probes match Python incl. domain edges and the documented C-style `divmod`; CSV matches Python's `csv` on 12/13 hard RFC-4180 cases (13th documented); `path` is Python-exact where it claims Python and Go-exact where it claims Go, 21 edge cases |
| `std.duration` formatting | byte-identical to Go `time.Duration.String()` across 14 magnitudes incl. `59m59.999s` and `1m29.5s`. (The **parser** is W8-9) |
| RE2 regex | **no ReDoS** — *re-measured here, and the report's repro was WRONG*: `(a+)+$` against exactly 30 `a`s returns in **0.000 s in CPython too**, because it MATCHES immediately. The catastrophic case needs a non-matching tail. Corrected repro, Linux: subject `"a"*30 + "b"` → **CPython `re` 86.42 s**, **Chezzi 0.000077 s** (`Ok(false)`). The finding is real and larger than reported; only its repro was mis-stated |
| netpoller | measurably parks — a 300 ms socket read while a sibling counter keeps ticking, at default and `--threads=1`; 20 concurrent connections correct at every worker count; split-codepoint reassembly byte-exact; a binary payload is a sticky self-explaining `Err` that `read_bytes` recovers losslessly |
| concurrency correctness | 20/20 race runs, zero lost updates across `AtomicInt`/`Atomic`/`Shared`/`RwShared`; all three deadlock shapes detected in ms with rc=1 **and better messages than Go**; `recover:` around a nursery is a free errgroup; `pmap` ran 8×50 ms sleeps in 51 ms; Channel close/range/send-on-closed/recv-on-closed and bounded backpressure all correct |
| FFI safety | beats `ctypes` on three axes — a faulting Chezzi comparator inside libc `qsort` becomes a recoverable `Err` (CPython prints a traceback, `qsort` returns normally, array left unsorted, exit 0); interior NULs caught (`ctypes` silently returns 2 for `b"ab\x00cd"`); a stored callback aborts loudly instead of jumping to freed memory |
| generators | genuinely lazy — `islice(naturals(), 5)` over `while true` terminates, with an interleaved produce/consume trace proving pull-based evaluation; partial `for` + `break` then resume continues correctly; self-re-entrancy is `Err('generator already running')` |
| `chezzi test` | stood up a live TCP server with 20 concurrent clients **inside a `test fn`** — no framework, no plumbing; 9 tests across two projects green at two worker counts, three consecutive runs, no flake |
| scaffold & CLI | best `init` from a young language (the generated comments teach the model); module-resolution errors print the whole import cycle and the exact path searched; every CLI misuse handled and worded well; exit codes correct everywhere checked |
| best-in-class messages | the binding-rule, witness-passing and `?`-mismatch diagnostics **name the fix verbatim** — *"Declare the type parameter on the MEMBER instead (`fn default_of[T: <bound>](self, ...)`)"*, *"'?' propagates a None, but the enclosing function returns Result, not Option"*, *"stream did not contain valid UTF-8 — use io.read_bytes for binary files"*. **This is the bar the rest of the diagnostics should meet** (W8-13..W8-17) |

What is **not** in the same shape is everything around the semantics: **five ways to get a silently
wrong answer** (six with W8-6), **a scheduler whose default is its worst setting**, and **a diagnostics
layer that knows what is wrong and won't say what to do about it**.

### Real-app numbers (the reporters', darwin 10-core)

A log analyzer built in Chezzi and ported to Python produced **byte-identical output** in both text and
JSON mode, on 2k- and 500k-line inputs.

| input | Chezzi | Python 3.11 |
|---|---|---|
| 2,015 lines | **0.01 s** | 0.07 s |
| 50,375 lines | **0.07 s** | 0.11 s |
| 503,750 lines | 0.54 s | 0.53 s |
| startup | **0.00 s** | 0.06 s |

Chezzi wins at every realistic log size **on startup alone**, ties at 500k. Subtracting startup the
compute is ~1.15× slower than CPython — while Python's regex is C and its `ThreadPoolExecutor` is
GIL-serialized and Chezzi's `pmap` is genuinely parallel across 5 files. Per core the regex + string
path is doing materially more work; the parallelism closes the gap. **Note this number was taken with
W8-7/W8-8 live**, so it is a floor, not a ceiling. (Both closed 2026-08-18; the number has not been
re-taken since.)

LOC: logstat **206 Chezzi vs 73 Python** (2.8×, but ~40 lines of that is manual JSON construction —
**W8-20**; strip it and it is ~2.0×). kv server **164 Chezzi vs 115 Go** (1.4×) *despite* Chezzi
carrying an extra `Result`-threaded client module — `parallel:` beats `WaitGroup` + `once.Do` + a `done`
channel, and `write(f)` owning the guard makes a missing unlock unwritable.

### THE META-FINDING — none of W8-1..W8-17 was reachable by the standing gates

4375 Rust tests, 586 Chezzi tests at two worker counts, the CPython differential, and `cargo test
conformance` were **all green** while every one of these was live. That is not a gap in any one gate;
it is a statement about what the gates are shaped to see:

- **A silent wrong answer has no assertion to fail.** W8-2/W8-3/W8-4/W8-6 all return a plausible value
  and exit 0. A suite catches a wrong answer only where someone wrote down the right one — and nobody
  writes an assertion for behaviour they believe is impossible (a lost `Shared.set`, a discarded
  `Result`). This is the same shape as **`widening-untested-by-its-own-suite`**, one level up: *a
  behaviour nobody suspected is structurally untested by the suite written by people who did not
  suspect it.*
- **No gate measures performance.** W8-7 and W8-8 are pure timing facts. `benches/run.chz` measures
  single-task throughput, which is precisely the shape that cannot see either of them (W8-7 needs ≥2
  fibers in a scope to fire). (Partly addressed when those two closed: `tests/chezzi_threads_cli.rs`
  now asserts a >5.5× serialization ratio at `CHEZZI_THREADS=1` and the new
  `tests/chezzi_threads_sys_time.rs` asserts `sys < 0.03 * user` at the default worker count. Both are
  narrow gates over the two specific shapes; the general statement stands.)
- **No gate reads a message.** W8-13..W8-17 are all message-quality. The suite asserts *that* a
  diagnostic fires and often its exact text — never whether the text tells the reader what to do.
- **No gate executes prose.** All twelve W8-18 rows. `cargo test conformance` executes `grammar.bnf`
  and the goldens execute `examples/*.chz`, but a sentence in `stdlib.md` is unexecutable by
  construction, and **eight of the twelve were STALE rather than never-written** — they described
  behaviour that had since changed, which is exactly what CLAUDE.md's *"docs are part of the change,
  not a follow-up"* rule exists to prevent.
- **A detector scoped narrower than its surface reports success by silence.** W8-11: the FFI goldens
  are `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]`, so `cargo test` is green on a Mac **with the entire FFI surface
  unexercised**. Same family as **`lossy-decode-blinds-a-comparison-oracle`** and W6-9b — when the
  oracle can't see the case, absence of failure is not evidence of correctness.

**Carry into the freeze:** a green suite measures the assertions you thought to write. The two
detectors that *did* earn their keep here are the ones that compare against something outside this
repo — the CPython differential (which found the `NaN` byte and nothing else, because there was nothing
else) and running the actual Go/Python/Rust program, which is what produced W8-3, W8-4, W8-5, W8-7,
W8-8, W8-9 and W8-12. That is CLAUDE.md's ancestor rule paying out at scale, and it is the argument for
`docs/future.md` §2b's unbuilt **Go-paired-programs differential**.

### Reproduced on Linux, verbatim — the five silent wrong answers

All five return a plausible value; four of the five exit 0. (Ranked by how likely you are to ship one
without noticing.)

```
W8-1  print("\\d{4}-\\d{2}")        → \d4-\d2         (python3: \d{4}-\d{2})
W8-2  fn f(): g()                   → rc=0, silent    (top-level g() → unhandled error: E, rc=1)
W8-3  Shared(10), set(99) in update  → 11, rc=0        (docs said: self-deadlock)
W8-4  w.sort_by_key(bump)            → faults: list modified during 'sort_by_key' (CLOSED 2026-08-29)
W8-5  json.parse("["*100k+"]"*100k)  → rc=1, process dead, "still alive" never printed
W8-6  replace_all(…, r"\2/\1")       → Ok('\\2/\\1')   (the \1 form is not an escape in RE2) (CLOSED 2026-08-27)
```

Two corrections to the report as filed, recorded so nobody re-chases them: **W8-5's repro as written
does not compile** (there is no `std.text` module — `repeat` is a `str` method), and its frames point at
`line 43, col 9` of `std/json.chz`, not `line 170`. The finding itself is exact.

### Scheduler, and what it does to measurements taken elsewhere

Two CPU-bound tasks in one nursery, only `--threads` varying, Linux 12-core:

| `--threads` | real | user | sys |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **1.376** | 2.712 | 0.008 |
| 2 | 1.396 | 2.740 | 0.017 |
| 4 | 1.395 | 2.868 | 0.166 |
| 8 | 1.455 | 3.494 | 0.663 |
| 12 | 1.787 | 4.800 | 2.269 |
| **0 (default)** | **1.826** | 4.775 | **2.491** |

Monotone in worker count, and the **sys** column is the whole diagnosis: idle workers thrash rather
than sleep. Go's equivalent is 0.08 s at 0.00 sys at both `GOMAXPROCS=2` and `10`. And the `--threads=1`
floor (W8-8), 8 CPU tasks:

```
T=1  real 2.569  user 5.093  → 1.98 cores      (single-burn baseline at T=1: 0.589 s)
T=2  real 2.689  user 5.326  → identical to T=1
T=3  real 1.852  user 5.508  → 2.98 cores
Go GOMAXPROCS=1  0.51 s (really serializes)  ·  GOMAXPROCS=10  0.08 s
```

The tables above are **dated records of the pre-fix engine** (2026-08-17) and are kept verbatim.
**Both rows are CLOSED 2026-08-18** on `fix/mn-idle-policy-w8-8-w8-7`, in the filed order — W8-8 first,
because every `--threads=N` measurement in the tree meant something different until it landed. Post-fix,
`examples/primes_parallel.chz` on the same box (real/user/sys): T=1 15.301/15.327/0.236 (**1.00 cores**,
was 1.91), T=12 5.586/16.879/0.003 (sys was 10.729), default 5.961/18.475/0.009 (sys was 10.110) — the
default is no longer the slowest setting, and the monotone-in-worker-count curve is gone. Go
`GOMAXPROCS=1` measures 1.00 cores and Rust N=1 0.99 on the same box, all four programs printing
`primes below 2,000,000: 148933`; full tables in `docs/benchmarks.md` §"W8-7 / W8-8 idle-worker-policy
fix".

**The outstanding work this section filed — re-deriving every rationale built on a two-wide
`CHEZZI_THREADS=1` — is DONE (2026-08-18), and it is the part to read.** All **nine** claims were re-run

### ~~The airlock trap that turned a real test green while it asserted nothing~~ — **CLOSED 2026-08-17**

Documented behaviour (`syntax.md` §11b) — a write to a captured local inside `spawn:` does not escape
the task — but worth its own note because of the failure mode:

```chezzi
results: List[str] = []
parallel:
    spawn:
        results = pmap(ids, ...)
for r in results:            # ZERO iterations — every assertion inside is SKIPPED
    assert r == "ok"
```
```
inside task: results=['a', 'b'] n=7
after join:  results=[] n=0      (Go, same shape: after join: results=[a b] n=7)
loop iterations=0
```

The compiler **can see** a local written inside a task and read after the join. A warning there costs
nothing and prevents the failure mode that erodes trust fastest — a green test that tested nothing.
This is the same *correct > silent > wrong* ordering as **`parked-is-not-stuck`**, applied to a check
rather than a verdict. Filed under W8-19's fix list rather than as its own row because the airlock
semantics are deliberate and unchanged; only the missing warning was at issue.

**CLOSED 2026-08-17 — the checker warns at the READ, and the airlock semantics are untouched.** The
repro above, verbatim, on the release binary:

```
warning (line 5, col 10): 'results' is read here as its pre-`spawn:` value — a captured binding
crosses the task airlock as an independent copy, so the write inside the `spawn:` block (line 4) is
not visible after the join (carry the value out on a Channel, or use a Shared)
iterations over 0
rc=0
```

Non-fatal, like its W8-2 sibling; the `Shared` rewrite of the same program is **silent** and prints
`2`. Four hooks, no dataflow pass: the taint is recorded once at the top of `check_assign`'s lvalue
`match` (so `xs[i] = v`, `p.f = v`, `a.b[0].c = v` all resolve to the binding that actually crosses,
and a fifth lvalue arm added later is covered without an edit), once in `infer_method_call` for an
in-place mutator, reported at the read in `infer_ident`, and taken/restored per frame in
`check_fn_body`.

**The warn/silent split IS a measured table, not a design.** Every shape was run on the pre-rule
binary and the rule follows what the parent actually observed after the join: reassigning a captured
local, `xs.push`, `xs[0] = 9`, `p.x = 9`, `m["a"] = 9`, the **module-top-level** form of the repro,
the implicit-nursery (bare `spawn:`) form, a captured module global, a spawn inside a `for` read after
the loop, and the two parent-side read-modify-writes (`xs = xs + [2]`, `n += 1` — measured `1`, not
`2`) all lose the write and all warn. `Shared.update`, `Channel.send`, a `defer:` block in the
**parent**, a task-local nested `fn`, and a parent overwrite that supersedes the task's write all
survive and stay silent. The handle-type exemption is not a second list to maintain: `mutates_receiver`
is keyed on the receiver **type**, so `Shared`/`RwShared`/`Atomic`/`Channel`/`Executor`/`Socket`/
`Listener`/`Writer`/`Reader` fall through — and `str.reverse` (returns `str`) vs `List.reverse`
(returns `nil`) is exactly why the key is the type and not the name.

**Two things measurement inverted while building it**, both recorded because they are what a
re-derivation would get wrong: (1) the "locals only" line the note implied is drawn in the wrong
place — at **module top level** the binding is scope 0, so the filed repro *verbatim* would not have
warned; the rule uses `is_captured`, not `is_local_capture`. (2) The `defer:` claim was backwards: it
is the **parent** `defer:` that is exempt (its write IS visible — measured `1`), while a `defer:`
nested inside `spawn:` is on the far side of the airlock and correctly taints.

**Seven deliberate ceilings, all under-warns, all pinned by tests so closing one fails loudly**
(`ponytail:` markers in `src/checker/`, numbered list in `syntax.md` §11b, same seven in
`concurrency.md`): per **frame**, so the taint crosses no `fn` boundary in either direction (a
*closure* body is an expression in the parent's frame and so still warns — measured, and deleting that
was a true positive a first cut nearly threw away); lexical order, not dataflow; builtin containers
only, so a user struct method that mutates `self` is invisible; re-declaring the name clears the taint
(which is what stops a merely-shadowing loop variable being reported — and the taint **does** carry a
scope coordinate, so a *block-local* shadow's taint dies with its block instead of being charged to the
outer binding); a partial parent-side `m[k] = v` / `p.f = v` untaints silently (it *may* supersede the
task's write and the checker cannot tell which — `parked-is-not-stuck`: decline rather than warn on
noise); a body declared inside the task is not summarized back to its call site; and, the mirror of the
partial-write rule, **a partial read of a partial write declines** (a task-side `p.count = …` read back
as `p.name` names a part the checker cannot match up, so `p.count` read back as `p.count` is missed —
the three mixed pairs still report, because there it *can* tell).

**The last two ceilings exist because the first cut OVER-warned, and it took an adversarial pass to
find it.** Both shapes were false warnings on correct code: a block-local shadow's taint was charged to
the outer binding (`xs := [10,20]`, an inner `if` block re-declaring `xs := [1]` and spawning
`xs.push(99)`, warned at a post-block `print(xs.len())` that correctly prints **2**), and a
field-granular write poisoned every later read of the root — including in a program that had already
applied the fix the message recommends (task writes `p.count` **and sends it on a `Channel`**, parent
reads only `p.name` → warned, printing the correct `bob`/`1`). A warning that fires after the user did
exactly what it told them to do is worse than no warning. Both were caught only by two isolated
prosecutors and a defender, not by the suite; the code comment at the time asserted the opposite
invariant (*"Under-warning, never over-warning"*), which is precisely the shape a green suite cannot
contradict.

**Over-fire evidence, re-run on the release binary:** the `Shared` and `Channel` rewrites of the
repro, a 3-worker pool over a closed `Channel`, an `Executor` fan-out of 10 jobs into a `Shared` — all
silent. The whole `tests/chz` suite emits **zero** warning lines at both worker counts, including all
13 sites of `tests/chz/spec/airlock_shared_binding_test.chz`. Nothing was silenced to get there.

### Language milestones decided out of this pass (W8-21, W8-22) — NOT dogfood findings

Two design decisions came out of the W8-2 / W8-19 discussion on 2026-08-17. They are filed as rows so
the **rejected** alternatives and the ancestor survey survive, which is the part that rots first.

**W8-21 — success-coercion at `T?` / `T!E` sinks. CLOSED 2026-08-30 (TICKET-025).** The syntax already
shipped; the coercion is now implemented — a bare success value at a declared `T?`/`T!E` return sink
(a `fn`/closure return, incl. inline-expr body, and a bare `return` at `Result[nil, E]`) coerces to
`Some(v)`/`Ok(v)` via a checker-produced `RetCoerceTable` the type-blind compiler consumes verbatim at
its four return-sink lowerings. Decided: **exactly two coercions, both on the success side**
(`T`→`Some`, `T`→`Ok`). The proposal originally had a third, `E` → `T!E`, and killing it is the design
content:

| ancestor | coerces value → error-union? | how the overlap is avoided |
|---|---|---|
| Zig | yes | error side is an **error set** — a distinct kind, **no payload** (documented; not re-run, no toolchain here) |
| Swift / Kotlin / C# | optional only | errors live in `throws`/exceptions, absent from the return type |
| Rust | **no** | never offered — measured: `error[E0308]: expected \`Result<String, String>\`, found \`String\`` |
| Go | n/a | **position** decides, not type — measured: `("ok", nil)` / `("", boom)` |

**Nobody resolves the overlap; they all make it unrepresentable.** Zig buys the third rule by giving up
error payloads — Chezzi's `Error` has `.message()` and `E` is arbitrary, so that trade is already spent.
And the overlap here is not theoretical: `str` → `Error` is a **general** assignability rule (measured:
`e: Error = "boom"` compiles), so every `str` satisfies both sides of a `str!` sink — **34 sites**
(`Result[str]` ×19, `str!` ×15) against the 81 `return Err(` the rule would have saved. The replacement
is the **`!"..."`** sugar: the sigil supplies exactly the disambiguation types cannot.

**W8-22 — a caught `Error` carries its origin. CLOSED 2026-08-30 (TICKET-026).** The location already
existed and was discarded at one line (`src/vm/exec.rs:1392`, pre-fix); `e.line()`/`e.col()`/`e.file()`
now read it back. **The prescription this row originally recommended — a new native struct replacing
the `Err` payload — was measured wrong and was NOT built:** it breaks `e == "boom"` and the `Err('...')`
repr two suite tests assert. The payload stays `Obj::Str`; the origin rides in a `GcRef`-keyed side
table on `Heap`, stamped at the three `recover:` boundaries and pruned in `Heap::sweep`. The 336
`Err("...")` sites don't move, and neither does `==` or display for a user-constructed error. Ancestors
split evenly (Python yes, Zig debug-only, Rust and Go no), so this stayed a real choice; the shipped
shape is **construction span only, default rendering unchanged**, reusing `Program::file_path`,
`lexer::render_span` and `Program::modules` (the `Span.file` → path resolvers `W8-14`/`W8-15` landed).

### Verdict as reported

Nine of ten developers said they would ship on their area, each with a short blocking list. **The
language is further along than its diagnostics make it look:** the code that runs is right far more
often than the messages suggest, and where it diverges from its ancestors it usually diverges *upward*
— loop-scoped fresh cells, recoverable overflow, static bool conditions, `Option`-returning removals,
block-scoped `defer`, no ReDoS, no GIL. The gap between those two facts is W8-1..W8-20.

## Session log — 2026-08-16 (serial-engine removal: 2 rows closed, 1 dissolved, 6 fixes found doing it)

The `--serial` cooperative engine, the `--check-parity` flag, the cooperative scheduler and every
per-engine fork were **removed** (`docs/future.md` §2b — which shipped **pre**-freeze, reversing its own
"not before the JIT freeze" ordering). What follows is what the removal closed, and what it turned up on
the way. Every item below has a row in the OPEN ITEMS table.

**Closed BY the removal (nothing fixed — the divergent engine is gone):**
- **N10** — closed **for the cooperative fiber**. The surviving `op_wait_poll` inline-sleep arm is
  reachable on M:N and still sleeps to the deadline without re-polling siblings; see that section.
- **N6g** — dissolved. The C5 park limitation itself survives; only the divergence died.
- **W6-9r item 1** — its WON'T FIX rested on the ~60 cross-engine compare sites being scheduled for
  deletion. They were deleted. **Item 4 (the `captured()` DISPLAY boundary) stays OPEN on its own
  terms** — it is a property of the capture surface, not of the comparators.
  *(Superseded later the same day: item 4 was CLOSED 2026-08-16 — `chezzi test --show-output` writes
  `TestReport.bytes` byte-exactly. Kept as written because it records why the removal did not close
  it; the index row is the authority.)*

**Found and fixed WHILE doing it — four bugs the removal did not cause:**

### An `Executor` join waited for the joiner's own job — a healthy run reported a deadlock (`3f293c60`)

```chezzi
import std.concurrency
fn stop(e: Executor):
    e.shutdown_now()
fn main():
    ex := Executor()
    ex.submit(fn(): print("A"))
    ex.submit(fn(): stop(ex))
    ex.submit(fn(): print("C"))
    ex.shutdown()
    print("end")
main()
```

| binary | result |
|---|---|
| `target/debug/chezzi`, 60 runs, PRE-fix | **51× `A C end` rc=0, 9× (15%) `A C` then `runtime error: waiting for this Executor's jobs: deadlock` rc=1** |
| `target/release/chezzi`, 40 runs, PRE-fix | 40× `A C end` rc=0 — timing masks it |
| **CPython 3.14.6 `ThreadPoolExecutor` equivalent** | `A C end` rc=0, **every run** |
| post-fix, debug and release | **240/240 each, zero faults** |

Both `A` and `C` print first, so every job ran. **Root cause:** `join_eager_jobs` waited for
`outstanding()` to reach 0 **even when the waiting thread was itself one of the counted jobs**, so its
`PartyWait::Join` was never satisfiable and `quiesced_only_joins` declared a completed run dead. The
graceful `shutdown()` variant faulted **8/8** — the 15% figure above only looks like a race because the
`shutdown_now` cancel rung gives most runs an escape the graceful path does not have. **Fix:** discount
the joiner's own slot (`slack`) in the wait loop and in `Join` satisfiability — a self-join takes no
slots. The bounded `KNOWN_FLAKE` retry in `tests/executor_reentrant_shutdown.rs` was deleted with the
bug, since a test that retries past a real fault is papering over it.

**This is a fourth instance of the [[parked-is-not-stuck]] family** (with `W7-12`, `W7-56`, `W7-58`): a
runtime verdict that declares user code broken must be built from what is **impossible**, not from what
looks idle. Here the predicate could not have been satisfied by any schedule, because the party it was
waiting on was the party doing the waiting.

### A self-shut `Executor`'s slots were never reduced — buffered output lost, and a failing `assert` returned `Ok(())` (`3fb223ee`)

`drain_live_executors` read `shut` as "already handled", so an executor shut down from inside one of its
own jobs never had its outcome slots reduced. Two observable halves, **both red pre-fix, 150/150 after**:

- buffered job output **lost 10/10**;
- **a sibling job's failing `assert` made the run return `Ok(())`** — a silent wrong result on exactly
  the path a test runner reads to decide pass/fail. This is the worse half by a distance.

Fixed with `ExecutorCore::unreduced`, carrying an acknowledged `ponytail:` comment naming its ceiling (a
narrow window between setting `shut` and marking `unreduced`). Review verified `unreduced` is set and
cleared coherently and cannot double-reduce. A follow-up pass (`a084f3ca`) narrowed the bail-clear to
genuine self-joins, watchdogged the new test (it needs ≥2 pool threads, and hung >120 s under
`taskset -c 0` without one), and moved `executor_results_are_not_retained` to its own process after
root-causing its flake to `vm::pool` sharing rather than to the cap.

### The `EagerState` doc claimed an ordering guarantee that never existed — **the doc was the defect** (`3fb223ee`)

Filed as a runtime ordering bug **twice**, and both times the direction was wrong. `EagerState` was
documented as giving submission-ordered job output. Under `chezzi run` it never did and never could:
`HostConfig::stream` is written at exactly **one** site (`src/main.rs`, the `run` subcommand) and sends
every `print` to the real fd **at print time**, engine-wide. The submission-ordered per-slot flush
governs only the **buffered sink** that the in-process test helpers use.

| measured, with REAL work in each job | result |
|---|---|
| Chezzi nursery, `chezzi run` | printed **reversed 100/100** |
| CPython `ThreadPoolExecutor` | held submission order **0/30** |

So Chezzi already matched its owning ancestor and only the documentation disagreed. Corrected in
`src/vm/core.rs`, `docs/concurrency.md` and `docs/stdlib.md`.

**Why it was mis-diagnosed twice, which is the transferable part:** the control program used *trivial*
job bodies, where submission order survives by accident. **Before filing an ordering bug, run the
ancestor with realistic work** — a short task hides the very nondeterminism you are testing for.

### `List[Any]` widened an int to a float, at five positions (`ee13cf6f` → `5883dc98` → `da3a87fa`)

The tracked wave-4 gap (`Session log — 2026-07-23`), fixed. `xs: List[Any] = [1, 3.0]` stored `1.0` for
the int; CPython keeps `[1, 3.0]`. The type-blind `literal_numeric_mix` peephole widened an untyped int
const whenever a float const sibling existed, regardless of the checker-resolved element type — a
check-clean silent wrong value, invisible to any engine comparison because both engines had it.

Two things worth carrying forward:

1. **Grepping the SHAPE found a FIFTH position that enumeration had missed** — a struct-constructor
   argument. The four were listed from memory; the list was wrong. Same meta-finding this file already
   records under "a fix applied to SOME arms of an N-way set".
2. **The `if`/`match` scalar sibling was deliberately LEFT ALONE, and pushing back on the instruction to
   change it was correct.** Branches must unify, so the widen there is what *produces* the float that is
   later assigned into the `Any` slot; suppressing it would turn accepted programs into `branches have
   incompatible types: int and float`. **Rust rejects `if c {1} else {2.0}` outright**, so branch
   unification is ancestor-faithful — it is a different rule, not the same defect. (`Map[K, Any]` is
   invariant and rejects every mixed literal, so it has no site of the shape.)

The final shape rides **one** seam: every `expected_hint` set site feeds a single sink (`infer_kind`'s
`ExprKind::List` arm), so the checker records a per-literal verdict into a new `ListWidenTable` that the
type-blind backend consumes. `chezzi test` 552 → 565.

### …and that side table's key aliased two AST nodes — instance #4 of the span-keyed class (`da3a87fa`)

Adversarial review of `5883dc98` was pointed at the side table's injectivity **on purpose**, because
this file already tracks the hazard. It was real. `ListWidenTable`'s `carrier_key` aliased the
**synthesized variadic pack** onto a **piped list literal** — `desugar/mod.rs` gives the pack the CALL's
span, and a pipe gives that call the LHS primary's span:

```
vari([1, 3.0], 2.5, 1)          →  [[1.0, 3.0], 2.5, 1]
[1, 3.0] |> vari(2.5, 1)        →  [[1, 3.0],   2.5, 1]     # same program, different answer
```

A check-clean **silent wrong value**. Fixing it turned up a **third** shape the review had missed: two
synthesized packs in one pipe chain alias pack-to-pack
(`[1, 3.0] |> vari(2.5, 7) |> varif(1, 2.0)` → a hard `internal:` error on a valid program), which is
precisely why the fix carries the **callee's span** rather than a bool "is-a-pack" marker — two packs in
one chain are two coordinates, not one flag.

**Fixed by making the coordinate REAL, never by re-anchoring a span**: `ExprKind::List` gained an
`Option<Span>` origin (`None` for a user-written list, the callee's `witness_key_span` for the one
synthesized pack), so the key is `(CarrierKey, Option<Span>)`. Sweep result: exactly ONE synthesized
`List` node exists in the crate.

**The [[span-keyed-table-aliasing]] class now reads FOUR instances, not three: `M24-6`, `W7-49`,
`W7-43`, and this one.** That running count is the point of those rows — a checker→compiler side table
keyed on a `Span` aliases wherever the same AST is reachable under two identities (a spliced default, a
re-lexed fragment, a chained postfix link, and now a synthesized desugar node).

### The lib test suite was failing 8/8 on one assertion, and it was a pool, not the branch (`06ad7451`)

`src/vm/pool.rs` is **one process-wide `OnceLock` pool**. Under `RUST_TEST_THREADS=4` the
`chz_suite_passes` gate ran concurrently with ~4150 unrelated lib tests all contending for it, and one
embedded `tests/chz` case — `shutdown_now_interrupts_a_sleeping_job` — asserts a wall-clock bound
(`d < 1.0 s`, 3× headroom under the job's real 3 s deadline) on how fast a cancelled job's worker
notices the cancel. Measured: **8/8 full `cargo test --lib` runs failed this exact assertion**, `d`
landing 1.03–1.44 s — the cancel genuinely lands, just delayed by starvation. Filtering the test alone
inside the same binary already passed in 3.5 s, which is the fix made permanent: the gate moved to its
own binary `tests/chz_suite.rs`, and cargo runs test **binaries** one at a time.

Separately, `gc_tests::shared_box_survives_gc_stress` pinned an exact push order that **300 stress
iterations showed to be racy** (both orderings observed); relaxed to an order-independent GC-survival
check, which is what the test was actually for. **8/8 green after**, ~27.6–28 s per run.

**Standing rule this establishes: a test needing exclusive pool access belongs in `tests/`, not the lib
suite.** There are now four such binaries — `chz_suite.rs`, `chezzi_threads_cli.rs`,
`executor_results_not_retained.rs`, `executor_reentrant_shutdown.rs`.

**And what this was NOT.** An earlier characterisation of the same symptom blamed a *different* test
each run and read as branch flakiness (16/21 green over 21 runs). Re-run on a quiet host (load 0.94, 12
cores, no other session): **4153 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored, 3/3, ~28 s per run**, against ~257 s per
run under contention — a **9× wall-clock difference** traced to a second Claude session working in the
same repo. Load contention and a real single-cause bug are indistinguishable from the tally alone; both
were present, and only one of them was fixable.

### What replaced the oracle, stated without overclaiming

`docs/future.md` §2b promised four replacement oracles. **Two exist:** the CPython differential
(`src/difftest/`, pre-dating the removal and untouched by it) and a **new** two-worker-count schedule
differential (`tests/chezzi_threads_cli.rs`, task 5) that runs the whole `tests/chz` suite through the
built binary at the default worker count and again at `CHEZZI_THREADS=2`. **Two do not:** the Go
paired-programs differential and the seeded/interleaving M:N mode are **unbuilt and still planned**.
That is a real gap in race-finding coverage, not a formality, and it is why §2b stays in the file.

Task 5 also found that **`chezzi test` never read `CHEZZI_THREADS` at all** — only `cmd_run` did — so a
hand-measured "552/552 at both worker counts" had been a silent no-op proving nothing. Fixed with a
shared `apply_env_worker_count`, with a causal proof attached: on a documented "needs ≥2 pool workers"
repro, `CHEZZI_THREADS=1` genuinely times out while `=2` and the default fault fast. **A knob is not a
gate until you have shown it changes an outcome.**

## Checker / type system

### Generic methods on RESERVED built-in receiver types — turbofish + bodied-method inference (found 2026-07-22, **1a/1b/2 RESOLVED 2026-07-22**)

A *generic* method call (`recv.m[U](...)` or inference of `U`) works on a **user struct** receiver
(`Ty::Struct`) but was **broken when the receiver is a reserved built-in type** — `Ty::List`/`Map`/`Set`
/`Shared`/`RwShared`/`Atomic`/`Executor`/`Socket`/`Listener`/`Writer`/`Reader`. Three facets, all fixed:

- **FIX 1a — turbofish on reserved receivers (RESOLVED).** `method_has_own_type_params`
  (`src/checker/expr.rs`) gained reserved-receiver arms (look up `self.structs.get(bare)` like the
  `Ty::Struct` arm — the container/concurrency method tables are re-seeded there under bare names), so
  the member turbofish `[1,2,3].map[int](…)` and any bodied generic method are no longer rejected
  *"method 'map' takes no type argument(s)"*. Non-generic methods (`filter`) still correctly reject.
- **FIX 1b — bodied generic method inference on the 4 concurrency handles (RESOLVED).** The
  `Ty::Shared`/`RwShared`/`Atomic`/`Executor` arms now route a harvested method whose sig carries
  `type_params` through `infer_generic_method` (prepend the concrete receiver, since the harvest strips
  `self`) — verbatim mirror of the `Ty::List` arm. So a bodied `fn m[U](self,f:fn()->U)->U` opens `[U]`
  and infers `U` from the closure, instead of failing *"expected fn()->U, found fn()->int"*.
- **FIX 2 — bodied-method runtime dispatch on the 4 concurrency handles (RESOLVED).**
  `try_native_bodied_method` is now called from the `Shared`/`RwShared`/`Atomic`/`Executor` arms of
  `do_method_call` (`src/vm/call.rs`), mirroring the `Writer`/`Reader` arms (try-bodied BEFORE native; a
  miss falls through byte-identically). Closes the check-OK/run-fault gap for bodied methods on those
  handles. **(2026-07-22 hardening, `auto-task/unify-native-dispatch-prefix`)** the eight per-handle
  arms were then folded into ONE `match self.heap.get(h)` key-map in `do_method_call`, and the checker's
  reserved-handle arms into `resolve_native_handle_method` — so bodied dispatch can no longer be
  forgotten on a NEW handle (adding it to the one match auto-enables it). Behavior-preserving; the fold
  also drops the eight `if matches!` probes off the hot list/map/struct method path.

**Shipped proof:** `Executor.submit_result[T](self, f: fn() -> T) -> Channel[T]` (`std/concurrency.chz`)
— the FIRST bodied generic method on a native struct, exercising 1a/1b/2 end-to-end. `submit_task`
(`std/concurrency/task.chz`) now builds over it. Tested both engines
(`vm::tests::executor_submit_result_both_engines`, checker tests
`reserved_receiver_generic_method_turbofish_ok` / `executor_bodied_generic_method_infers_from_closure`).

**Residual (deliberately NOT done):**
- **list/map/set bodied methods stay unharvested by design.** FIX 1b/2 cover only the 4 concurrency
  handles; the hot `list`/`map`/`set` `core_method` arm (`src/vm/call.rs`) is deliberately left untouched
  (an extra per-call table probe on `list.push` in loops = M19 perf risk, and no bodied methods exist
  there). List/Map/Set still reject bodied methods at check, so no check-OK/run-fault divergence.
- **`ex.submit_task(f)` dot-form** (a bodied generic method returning a *user* `Task[T]`) still needs the
  deferred Task-placement/harvest change (Option A — move `Task` so `Executor` can name it as a return
  type without an import cycle). `submit_task(ex, f)` free-fn form remains the shipped API.

## NEXT-SESSION BACKLOG — sendability completeness (deferred from 2026-07-21)

Three items to make the airlock sendability model Go-consistent (Go sends interfaces + closures over
channels; Chezzi should too). All DEFERRED to their OWN future sessions — do NOT bundle. Each is its own
spec. Ranked by value ÷ risk. (Context: Task 1 "align serial" landed 2026-07-21, `serial == M:N` by
construction; these three finish the sendability story.)

### 1. Protocol sendable under **(a)** — "Task 2" — **DONE 2026-07-21**
**LANDED.** All user protocol existentials are now sendable (Go `chan interface` parity): `Channel[P]`,
protocol-typed spawn args / struct fields / `Ok`/`Err` payloads / returns all type-check. The change was
**one logic line**, not a widening-site sweep: `sendable_rec`'s `Ty::Protocol` arm → `true` (was the
hardcoded `sendable_bounded(p) == "Error"`, now deleted), and `assignable`'s Protocol arm keeps the
existing `&& self.sendable(a)` concrete-witness guard uniformly.
**Premise correction (the old note above was wrong on two points):** (1) `assignable`
(`src/checker/proto.rs`) is the SOLE concrete→Protocol widening chokepoint — every widening category
routes through it, so there was **no widening-site coverage risk** and no sweep to do. (2) The
"non-sendable floor is FFI/handles" framing was backwards: the CHECKER marks FFI/`Func`/handles
**sendable** (`Ty::Func`/handle types are sendable) — the RUNTIME airlock (`ensure_crossable` over
`has_handle`, `src/vm/{sched,wire}.rs`) is the real gate for a genuinely-unserializable witness (one
carrying an FFI handle, a mid-`recover:` generator), rejecting it recoverably and identically on
serial == M:N. Post-change `sendable_rec` returns `false` only for `Ty::Module` (near-unconstructible as
a value), so the witness-sendable clause is near-vacuous — protocols behave like every other type.
Genuine-rejection coverage moved to the runtime: `vm::parity_tests::ffi_handle_cannot_cross_airlock_three_engine`.
Decision record: `~/.claude/plans/2026-07-21-task2-protocol-sendable-decision.md`.

### 2. Recursive-local-fn sendability — **DONE (2026-07-21)**
A nested recursive `fn` (and a mutually-recursive closure pair) now CROSSES the airlock and computes
correctly on both engines — the reject diagnostic is gone. Implemented via identity-preserving airlock
serialization on the `Obj::Cell` + `Obj::Closure` arms: a new `WireValue::Backref(u32)` + an `id`
on the wire arms. (Item **A** below since GENERALIZED this to every container arm, so self-referential
DATA crosses too.) `to_wire_depth` threads a back-edge memo (`WireMemo` — a
`FxHashMap<GcRef,u32>` DFS-stack set + id counter); on a revisit of a Cell/Closure still on the serialize
stack it emits `Backref(id)` and stops. `from_wire` ties the knot: alloc a placeholder `Cell(Nil)`/
`Closure(captured=[Nil;n])` FIRST, register `id→GcRef`, recurse children, then `heap.get_mut`-patch —
memory-safe because `Heap::alloc` never collects (no GC between placeholder and patch) and `GcRef` is a
GC-traced index. The old `graph_reaches_handle` reject (both call sites + the fn) is deleted.

**Corrected premise (the pre-work brief was wrong):** there was NO pre-existing cycle-safe airlock
serializer to mirror — `WireValue`/`SnapValue` were owned Box/Vec TREES with no identity/placeholder arm,
and `examples/airlock_cycle.chz` REJECTED cycles (`maximum structural depth exceeded`), it never
round-tripped them. This is brand-new identity-preserving machinery. (Item **A** later extended it to
container arms, and `airlock_cycle.chz` now ROUND-TRIPS — see below.) **Design deviation from the literal
task spec (recorded):** the memo is BACK-EDGE-ONLY (pops a node off the stack on DFS exit), so only a TRUE
cycle earns a `Backref`; an acyclic DAG alias (e.g. one arg `[f, f]`) is re-serialized as an independent
deep copy — preserving the documented Cell/closure deep-copy-independence contract (`wire.rs` §F1). A
plain visited-set (the literal spec) would have SHARED such aliases, a silent regression. Byte-identical
to the spec on every genuine-cycle case (self-recursion, mutual recursion, recursive-closure-capturing-an-
outer-local). **(SUPERSEDED by item A:** originally Struct/List/Map/etc. earned NO id — a pure-data cycle
tripped the depth cap; item A gave every container arm an id + `Backref`, so self-referential data now
round-trips too and `airlock_cycle.chz` FLIPPED to crossing.) Tests: `airlock_recursive_local_fn_round_trips_
both_engines` + `_under_gc_stress`, `airlock_mutually_recursive_pair_round_trips`, `airlock_recursive_
closure_captures_outer_local_round_trips`, `airlock_aliased_closure_stays_independent`, `generator_
carrying_recursive_closure_round_trips_both` (and `generator_parked_slot_nonsendable_rejects_both`
repointed by item A to a >10000-deep ACYCLIC parked slot, which stays a both-engines depth-cap reject).

### 3. Reject-case generators — mid-`recover:` (arm b) DONE; pending-`defer`/multi-frame (arms a,c) checker-unreachable
**Arm (b) — suspended mid-`recover:` — DONE (2026-07-21).** A generator suspended inside a `recover:`
block (a live handler stack in its parked context) now CROSSES the airlock and RESUMES with its recover
boundary intact. A `Handler` (`src/vm/mod.rs`) is pure plain-data (all `usize`, `Copy`, no `GcRef`/`Value`),
so it serializes as-is on `WireGenState::Suspended` (`src/vm/wire.rs`) with no value recursion; `from_wire`
rebuilds the frame/stack coherently so the handler indices stay valid. `generator_next` (`src/vm/exec.rs`)
rebases every parked frame's / handler's `nursery_len` to the resuming driver's floor at swap-in — a
generator provably opens no nursery of its own (`spawn`/`parallel:` are checker-banned inside a generator,
recover blocks included), so its escape-drain must be a no-op; this makes the stale cross-heap `nursery_len`
inert and also fixes a latent SAME-HEAP over-drain (resuming a mid-`recover:` generator at a deeper nursery
floor than it was first driven wrongly cancelled the driver's live sibling `spawn`s). Tests (`src/vm/
parity_tests.rs`): `generator_recover_suspended_resumes_both`, `generator_crossed_recover_catches_fault_
matches_control_both` (+ its inline `generator_recover_fault_control_inline` control — the item-#2 semantic
guard: the resumed recover must CATCH and produce the correct recovered value, matching a no-airlock
control), `generator_crossed_recover_fault_leaves_siblings_intact_serial` (the rebase, serial oracle).

**Arms (a) multi-frame + (c) pending-`defer` — NOT built; CHECKER-UNREACHABLE by construction; clean
reject KEPT as a defensive guard.** (a) `yield` only fires in a generator's own body frame (`in_generator`
resets at every fn/closure boundary), so a suspended generator always has exactly one frame — no
checker-valid source constructs a multi-frame suspension. (c) `defer` is banned inside a generator body
(`checker::sig`: "`defer` is not supported inside a generator", recover blocks recursed into), so a parked
frame can never carry a pending `defer`. The `to_wire` rejects (`src/vm/sched.rs`) stay as belt-and-braces
guards against the type-blind compiler path (the parity harness `run_program_inner` compiles WITHOUT the
checker); there is no coherent state to serialize, so nothing is built. Reject test kept:
`generator_parked_defer_rejects_clean_both`. Both engines reject IDENTICALLY (completeness, not a bug).

## NEXT-SESSION BACKLOG — sendability CONSISTENCY carve-outs (deferred from 2026-07-21)

After the 3 items above landed, the airlock is ~99% complete. Auditing "what's still unsendable" surfaced
that the genuinely-FUNDAMENTAL limit is only ONE thing — **a value carrying a live host handle**
(`Obj::Module`/`Obj::Native`/`Obj::Cffi` → `has_handle` → `ensure_crossable` "module/native/FFI handle
cannot cross"). A foreign OS/library resource cannot be memcpy'd into another heap; this is correct and
stays. (The concurrency handles `Channel`/`Shared`/`RwShared`/`Atomic`/`Executor`/`Socket`/`Listener`/
`Reader`/`Writer` cross as shared `Arc` cores; `ptr` crosses by value — none are in this set.)

The OTHER two remaining rejects are **arbitrary carve-outs**, not fundamental limits — the
identity-preserving `WireMemo`/`Backref` machinery built for recursive-fn sendability (item 2 above) can
close both, and doing so removes exactly the kind of "why can THIS cross but not THAT?" drift the no-drift
north-star forbids. Each is its OWN spec/session — do NOT bundle. Ranked by value ÷ risk.

### A. Self-referential DATA sendable — extend `Backref` to container arms — ✅ DONE (2026-07-21)
**LANDED.** Every container `WireValue` arm (`List`/`Tuple`/`Map`/`Set`/`Struct`/`Enum`/`NewType`/`Iter`)
now carries a per-serialization `id` + a `Backref` exactly like `Cell`/`Closure`, so a self-referential
struct/list/map (`a.next = b; b.next = a`) ROUND-TRIPS across the airlock (`spawn` arg / `Channel.send` /
`Shared` / module-global snapshot) instead of tripping `maximum structural depth exceeded`. `to_wire_depth`
inserts each container's GcRef into the `WireMemo` DFS stack BEFORE recursing (back-edge → `Backref(id)`,
removed on DFS exit so an off-stack DAG alias stays an independent deep copy); `from_wire_memo` ties the
knot in every container arm (placeholder-alloc → register `id` → recurse → `heap.get_mut`-patch). This was
a **net-deletion** change: the `WireMemo.nonpreserved_depth` machinery + BOTH mixed-cycle guards (commit
e8dcad7) are GONE — a mixed struct+closure cycle now just round-trips. **CORRECTION to the original spec
premise:** the note "`from_wire` already threads the `rebuild` map through every container arm, so the
tie-the-knot reconstruction is largely in place" was **WRONG** — the container arms recursed children
BEFORE alloc, so a nested `Backref` would have hit an unregistered id; the `from_wire` rewrite (every arm
placeholder-allocs + registers before recursing) was the bulk of the work. `examples/airlock_cycle.chz` +
its golden now ROUND-TRIP (sections 1-3); the depth cap STAYS as the backstop for genuinely-unbounded
ACYCLIC nesting (section 4 control + `generator_parked_slot_nonsendable_rejects_both`, re-pointed at a
>10000-deep acyclic parked slot). The **sole** remaining non-identity-preserved container is `Generator`
(its parked frame holds no `WireValue` id, so it can't back-reference) — a cycle threaded through a
generator is caught by the `WireMemo.gens_on_stack` guard (re-entering the same generator on the
serialize DFS stack → clean `a generator cannot be sent across tasks as part of a reference cycle`
reject, NOT a silent duplicate: once the containers back-reference, the container back-edge cuts the
recursion before the depth cap would trip, so the generator arm must guard the cycle itself). Tests:
`airlock_self_ref_{struct,list,map}_round_trips_both`, `airlock_mixed_struct_closure_cycle_round_trips_both`,
`airlock_struct_dag_alias_stays_independent` (adversarial parity-blind independence),
`airlock_self_ref_struct_round_trips_under_gc_stress`, `airlock_cyclic_module_global_crosses_mn`,
`generator_in_data_cycle_rejects_both` + `suspended_generator_in_data_cycle_rejects_both` (the
gen+container cycle reject). `src/vm/{wire.rs,sched.rs,fxhash.rs,core.rs,stmt.rs}`.

### B. Module-GLOBAL live generator sendable by value — ✅ DONE (2026-07-21)
**LANDED.** A module-global live generator now crosses the airlock BY VALUE (deep copy), exactly like a
frame-local one (F3 path C) — the reach-gate + Option-B poison→`nil` model is RETIRED. `to_snap_depth`'s
fast path no longer excludes generator-embedding values (`!value_embeds_generator` clause dropped), so a
handle-free module-global generator with all-sendable parked slots rides the `SnapValue::Wire(to_wire…)`
lane. Its slow `Obj::Generator` arm, however, must **NOT** re-raise the `to_wire` reject: `snapshot_modules`
walks EVERY module global of a nursery's snapshot, reached or not, so eager-faulting there aborts any
program that merely *holds* a non-sendable module-global generator it never sends (a regression vs the old
poison→`nil`-then-reach-gate model). Instead the slow arm snapshots a non-sendable generator (non-sendable
parked slot / reference cycle / parked host handle) as an inert **`Nil` placeholder** — the untouched-global
program runs CLEAN, and a task that REACHES it faults recoverably at the use site (`cannot iterate over nil`),
byte-identical serial == M:N. (Fault only when reached — the "when reached" contract; the frame-local F3
path-C crossing still rejects eagerly at `to_wire` because it only crosses the value actually sent.)
Each task already snapshots every module global per-task (`ensure_snapshot`, both engines since `6dca22c`),
so two tasks reaching the same SENDABLE module-global generator each drive their OWN independent copy —
memory-safe because `from_wire` rebuilds a fresh `GeneratorCore` on the worker heap (no shared cross-heap
`GcRef`); a non-sendable one is inert `Nil` on every worker, so no cross-heap handle can escape either.
**Net-deletion:** the whole reach-gate machinery is gone — `check_task_generator_reach`,
`check_outer_pending_generator_reach`, `check_task_reach_conservative`, `scan_proto_reaches_generator`,
`proto_reaches_generator(+_rec)` and its resolve/scan helpers, `any_hook_reaches_generator`,
`any_module_global_embeds_generator`, `module_slot_embeds_generator`, `value_embeds_generator`, the
`gate_executor_queue` executor path, and the `has_generators` VM field. (The `SnapValue::Poison` variant is
gone too; the inert placeholder reuses `SnapValue::Wire(WireValue::Nil)`.)
**CORRECTION to the original spec premise:** the "serial=shared-ref vs M:N=by-value-copy divergence" that
rated this MED-HIGH (why the `value_embeds` clause + `Poison` were kept, commit `7b73e7c`) was STALE after
`6dca22c` — the serial engine ALSO snapshots module globals per-task via the same memoized
`ensure_snapshot`/`to_snap`, so a per-task by-value generator copy is `serial == M:N` by construction.
Tests: `generator_module_global_{reached_crosses,suspended_reached_resumes,two_tasks_independent_copies,
parked_slot_nonsendable_rejects,in_data_cycle_rejects,unreached_nonsendable_runs_clean,via_executor_crosses}_both`
+ `generator_cross_module_member_call_crosses_both` (`src/vm/parity_tests.rs`). The memories
`generator-airlock-option-b-reach-gate` + `airlock-sendability-architecture` describe the retired model.

### NOT on the backlog (settled — not limitations)
- **Module handles** (a `Module`'s mutable globals in a value) — fundamental, stays rejected. Correct.
  Also source-unreachable (`module` is not a nameable type), so it's a defensive-only runtime guard.
  (Native `Obj::Native` + FFI `Obj::Cffi` fn values are NO LONGER here — they are pure code and now
  cross the airlock BY VALUE / shared `Arc`, exactly like a builtin fn; see the 2026-07-23 session log.)
- **Multi-frame / pending-`defer` suspended generators** — checker-UNREACHABLE (item 3 arms a/c); no valid
  program constructs them. The rejects are defensive guards, not a user-visible limit — nothing to build.

## Session log — 2026-07-28 (bug-hunt wave 7 — batch A: 3 host-boundary findings, ALL FIXED, no open rows)

Three defects at the **host boundary** (the native/CLI seam where raw OS bytes become Chezzi values) —
one P0 data-loss, two P1 host-panics. All three are fixed in this batch; **batch A adds NO row to the
OPEN ITEMS table**. Batch A deliberately does NOT fix the separately-filed **lossy path DECODE**
(`fs.list_dir`/`walk`/`glob`/`canonicalize`, `os.getcwd` decode a directory entry lossily and hand back a
path that does not exist) — it is uncoupled from these three and was its own later task, filed as
**W7-8** and **FIXED 2026-07-31**.

- **W7-1 (P0, DATA LOSS) — `fs.copy(p, p)` truncated the file to 0 bytes and returned `Ok(nil)`. FIXED.**
  `std::fs::copy` opens the DESTINATION `O_TRUNC`, so a self-copy wiped the file and reported success —
  check-OK, run-OK, data gone, byte-identical on both engines (parity-blind, like most of wave 6). It
  also fired when the two paths reached one inode through a **symlink**, so a path-string compare is not
  a fix. `copy` (`src/native/fs.rs`) now guards on **inode identity** (`dev`+`ino` via
  `MetadataExt`, `canonicalize` on non-unix) BEFORE the copy and returns a recoverable
  `Err("{from} -> {to}: are the same file")`, leaving the bytes untouched — matching Python
  `shutil.copyfile`'s `SameFileError` and coreutils `cp a a`. A missing destination is never "the same
  file", so copy-to-a-new-path is unchanged. `rename` needs no guard (POSIX `rename(p,p)` is a no-op);
  `copy` is the only truncating *pair* in the tree. Pinned by `tests/chz/stdlib/fs_copy_test.chz`
  (4 tests: same-path, symlink, plus two controls) on both engines.
- **W7-6 (P1) — a non-UTF-8 CLI argument or script path host-panicked the CLI, rc=101. FIXED.**
  `std::env::args()` PANICS on a non-UTF-8 item, so `chezzi run hello.chz "$(printf 'A\xffB')"` aborted
  at `library/std/src/env.rs:876` **before the program started**, on both engines, regardless of imports
  — a HOST panic, so `recover:` could not see it. `src/main.rs` now uses `args_os()` + a lossy decode.
- **W7-7 (P1) — a non-UTF-8 environment variable host-panicked at startup, rc=101. FIXED.**
  Same shape one layer down: `HostConfig::from_process` snapshots the whole environment with
  `std::env::vars()`, which panics at `env.rs:162` on one hostile variable — killing even a
  `print("hi")` program that never touches `std.os`. `src/native/mod.rs` now uses `vars_os()` + a lossy
  per-key/value decode. `os.environ`'s **sorted-by-key** lowering is downstream (`src/vm/mod.rs`) and was
  not touched; re-verified by running its existing golden.

**Decoding rule chosen (documented in `docs/stdlib.md`, not silent):** argv and env reach Chezzi as
`str`, so they are decoded **lossily** (invalid byte → `U+FFFD`; two raw env keys can collide, last
wins). The bar this batch sets is "the CLI never host-panics on hostile bytes", not byte-fidelity.
**v1 ceiling, stated:** a script whose PATH is not valid UTF-8 still cannot be RUN — it now fails
cleanly (`cannot read '…'`, rc=1) instead of rc=101. Threading a real `OsString`/`PathBuf` through
would change `read_source`/`type_check`/module-graph-root signatures (resolver + checker), out of scope
for a host-boundary batch.

**Same meta-finding as wave 6 (an N-way set, fixed on only some arms):** the two panicking calls had
**three** siblings, not two — `src/bin/difffuzz.rs` and `src/bin/panicfuzz.rs` carried the identical
`std::env::args()`. Swapped too (dev-only drivers, no test); `grep -rn 'std::env::args()' src/` and the
`vars()` equivalent now return zero live call sites, which is the guard.

### THE META-FINDING — 5 of the 6 P0s are ONE class: a fix applied to SOME arms of an N-way set

- W6-3: `compare`/`str` intercepted on scalar receivers, the other ~9 intrinsic protocol grants not. **FIXED.**

- W6-4: R1 swept `Socket`/`io`/`request`/`crypto` off `from_utf8_lossy`, missed `std.process`. **FIXED.**

### W6-1. `Writer.close()`/`flush()` on a `buffered` writer SILENTLY DOES NOT PERSIST — durability contract broken — P0 — **FIXED (2026-07-25)**
```chezzi
import std.io
fn main():
    match io.create("min.txt"):
        Ok(w0):
            w := io.buffered(w0, 4)
            w.write("abcdefgh")                      # 8 bytes > cap 4 -> mid-write drain
            print("close =", str(w.close()))         # Ok(nil)
            print("file  =", str(io.read_file("min.txt")))   # Ok()   <- EMPTY
        Err(e): print(e.message())
main()
```
Both engines, rc=0. Persists correctly **iff the buffer never filled**: cap4/len3 → `Ok(abc)`; cap4/len4,
len5, len8, cap1/len2, cap0 → all empty after a *successful* `close()`. Same for `flush()`. The bytes only
reach the fd when the heap is dropped at process exit, so an in-program reader, a `process.cmd` child, or a
sibling process sees a truncated/empty file after `close()` returned `Ok`, and a SIGKILL/abort after
`close()` loses the data outright — the exact guarantee `flush`/`close` exist to provide.
Reference (Python owns buffered-file semantics; Go `bufio` identical):
`python3 -c "f=open('py.txt','wb',buffering=4); f.write(b'abcdefgh'); f.close()"` → file is `b'abcdefgh'`.
**Root cause** `src/vm/fileio.rs:88-96`: the `Backing::Buffered` arm of `flush_core` returns `None` when
`buf.is_empty()`, short-circuiting the `self.flush_core(&inner)` at `:101` that the non-empty path DOES run.
A mid-write drain (`write_to_core`, `:58-64`) pushes bytes into the inner `BufWriter<File>` **without
flushing it** and empties `buf`, so the later `close()` flushes nothing; `close()` drops only the outer
`Backing::Buffered` (the program still holds `w0`, so the inner `WriterCore` isn't dropped either).
**Docs contradicted:** `docs/stdlib.md:415` (`close` = "Flush + close the handle"), `:417` ("Forgetting
`flush`/`close` … loses the tail — Go's footgun. Mitigated…"), and `flush_core`'s OWN doc-comment
("`Buffered` → drain the in-VM buffer to the inner core, THEN flush the inner (so `buffered(create(f))` is
